findings.where: Article specimen, body: the two opening paragraphs, the paragraph after the subhead, the closing 'So, to return…' paragraph and the three-item numbered list, at both widths (worst in the list at desktop-05 and phone-04)
findings.fault: The body text is centred. Every line starts somewhere different, so a long paragraph has no left edge for the eye to come back to. The heading, byline and caption above and beside it are left-aligned, so the column has two axes. In the list the numbers hang at the left but the item text is centred under them. Item 2's text starts well to the right of its number and item 3's starts further still, so the numbers don't line up with their items and the list reads as loose fragments.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff reading one of Mark's articles to judge his thinking: centred multi-line prose is slow and tiring to track. Angélique would also object: every article she adds would inherit this, and the brief makes the article specimen 'the product' and the proof that the rhythm holds her lists.

findings.where: The 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' / Subscribe band directly below the hero (desktop-02 top; phone-01 middle)
findings.fault: The second action is set as heavily as the first. It is a full-width saturated blue band with a display heading almost the size of Mark's line at desktop and larger than it on the phone (about 60 px against 38 px). The heading is centred where the hero is left-aligned. Squint at the phone and the newsletter wins over Mark's own line and his 'Write to me directly' action.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose test asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark and one message and one action leading. A visiting bank officer scrolling the phone would also object: they meet a louder subscription pitch than the invitation to write to Mark, and it looks like a marketing funnel, not a personal advisor.

findings.where: Hero lockup, top left, both widths: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark
findings.fault: His name is set small and light (about 20 px). The aqueduct mark beside it is larger, bolder and takes more width, so at a glance the firm's mark leads the lockup and the name reads as a small label next to it.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the personal-advisor test says his name leads with the logo beside it. Here the logo wins the pair visually, which leans back towards 'the firm is the brand'.

findings.fault: The photograph shrinks to a floating cut-out head squeezed between the nav and the heading. The logo's arches sit almost on the crown of his head, and the first line of the heading runs straight across his collar and jacket. Head, logo and heading collide in about 300 px, with no clear space between figure and words.
findings.who_objects: The founder and any phone visitor: on the phone the 'photograph is the hero' direction becomes a crowded stack where Mark's face looks pasted between the logo and the text, and the photograph loses the weight the advisor test asks for.

findings.where: Hero, bottom left, both widths: the 'Placeholder: Mark's photo…' note
findings.fault: The note about the photograph sits at the foot of the text column, under the action and far from the photo. Grouped by proximity with the words, it reads as a footnote to the action, not as a label on the picture.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the first screen: the stray small line under the action adds clutter to the column that should end on the one action.

findings.where: Section labels below the fold: 'PALETTE', 'Type pair', 'Texture', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch'
findings.fault: The peer section labels are each set differently: blue tracked capitals, a small bold sans, a large italic serif, then a small bold sans again. The sections fail similarity, so they don't read as a matched set, and 'Texture' outranks its siblings for no reason.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile: the style-tile parts look assembled rather than designed as one system, which weakens the case that the look is coherent.

findings.where: Below-fold specimen columns at desktop: Texture (two photos and the note in the left half, right half empty), the article specimen (notes stop high at right, then a long empty right column beside the photo, list and PDF card), the motion sketch (left column ends while the table and replay run on alone at right)
findings.fault: Each two-column section leaves one column empty for most of its height, so the lower page lurches left and right and has large dead areas, with no shared rhythm between sections.
findings.who_objects: The founder scrolling the specimen: the lower page looks unfinished and lopsided next to the composed hero.

findings.where: Palette's text-pair table on the phone (phone-02)
findings.fault: The table is squeezed into three narrow columns. Ratios break mid-value ('11.66 :' / '1'), and each pair's name wraps under its 'Aa' chip, so the rows read raggedly.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the tile on a phone: broken values look careless in a specimen that is meant to show care.
